findings.headline: 30.8% 99215 vs 4.3% expected; 7 of 10 documented 99215s in a random sample support a lower level
findings.interpretation: Highest risk-adjusted score in the book (21.2). 99215 share is high even for patients with 0–1 chronic conditions (21–26% vs 2–4% for peers). Random sample of 30 came back complete: 9 of 30 charts support a lower level than billed, including 7 of 10 99215s (peers: 25%). Draft overpayment estimate from the random sample is $24,843 (CI $15,722–$33,964). This needs coder review; it is not a finding.

findings.headline: 45.6% 99215 vs 8.2% expected; 9 of 13 documented 99215s support a lower level
findings.interpretation: The panel is somewhat sicker than average, but the 99215 share is far above peers at every complexity level. The full random sample of 30 arrived after one follow-up: 11 of 30 charts support a lower level than billed. Draft estimate $3,464 (CI $2,415–$4,513). Small volume (241 claims).

findings.headline: 15.9% 99215 vs 2.4% expected; 7 of 9 documented 99215s support a lower level
findings.interpretation: About half of the 99215s are on patients with 0–1 conditions. 45 charts on file in total (the 30-chart random sample plus earlier records): 10 support a lower level than billed, mostly 99215s documented as moderate or low MDM. Draft estimate from the random sample is $1,732 (CI $1,200–$2,264). Small dollar amount. Only 9 documented 99215s, so a human should confirm.

findings.headline: High 99215 share driven by a very complex panel; 0 of 30 random charts below billed
findings.interpretation: 915 of 2,402 visits are for patients with 5+ conditions. The 99215 share is low for healthy patients (5.6%). The full random sample arrived after a follow-up, and every chart supported the level billed (peer rate of charts below billed: 25%).

findings.headline: 99215 share rises with patient complexity; charts mostly support billing (2 of 30 below)
findings.interpretation: The 99215 share is near peer levels for 0-condition patients (3.9% vs 2.1%) and concentrated in 4+ condition patients. The 99215 share is still about 1.6–2.8x peers at each level, so this lean is moderate, but the random chart sample does not show upcoding.

findings.headline: 99215 share 10x expected, mostly on healthy patients; charts mostly support the codes, but some notes claim data review the claims do not show
findings.interpretation: 65% of 99215s are on patients with 0–1 conditions. Random sample of 30: only 3 below billed (2 of 8 99215s, the same as peers). But 6 of 19 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review have no lab or test line on the claim. This could mean notes written up to match the bill, so the charts are weak evidence either way. Recommend a coder look at whether the notes are copied forward. Not referred for recovery.

findings.headline: 99215 share 5x expected, including on 1-condition patients; charts support billing (1 of 30 below)
findings.interpretation: The claims pattern is elevated at every complexity level, but the random chart sample supports the levels billed. Not enough to lean either way.

findings.headline: 24% 99215 vs 3.4% expected; 2 of 30 random charts below billed
findings.interpretation: High 99215 share on low-complexity patients, but the charts do not show a lopsided pattern and there were few documented 99215s. Small volume (245 claims).

findings.headline: 22% 99215 vs 2% expected, mostly on healthy patients; only 12 of 30 charts returned
findings.interpretation: The review rule flagged 2 of 12 returned charts as below billed. But the office returned only some charts and did not answer the follow-up, so the returned set may not be representative and the sample is too small. The missing charts are not evidence of upcoding. The claims pattern is worth watching; consider asking again later.

findings.headline: 26.8% 99215 vs 2% expected, including on 0–1 condition patients; no records received
findings.interpretation: The office asked which visits were wanted and then did not answer the clarification. Request closed. Non-response is not evidence. The claims pattern is a concern, but nothing can be judged from charts.

findings.headline: Elevated 99215 share concentrated in complex patients (claims only)
findings.interpretation: The 99215 share for 0-condition patients matches peers (2.3% vs 2.1%). The excess is in 3+ condition patients. No records requested.
